newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia three-month KLIBOR fixed at 11.15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia three-month KLIBOR fixed at 11.15 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) was fixed at 11.15 percent at 0300 GMT.
It was at 8.38 percent on Thursday.
The one-month KLIBOR was fixed at 15.9 percent against 9.0 percent on Thursday.
KLIBOR is fixed by taking an average of rates offered by various banks in the country.

Money market dealers said the rise in interbank rates was triggered by a sudden tightening of liquidity in the system as a result of Bank Negara's massive intervention in the foreign exchange market earlier this week to help the ringgit.
"The rise was expected after the overnight rate jumped to 50 percent yesterday," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. The overnight was at 8.0 percent on Wednesday.
Dealers said more outflow of funds was expected on Friday from settlement of central bank intervention.
Although the actual size of the intervention was not known, dealers were estimating between 2.5 billion and 5.0 billion ringgit.
Bank Negara said on Wednesday that it would allow interest rates to rise as part of a move to curb speculation in the ringgit.
Dealers said they expected the overnight to remain high although it could fall back to around 40 percent.
